text:
Priya: customer FrostApps opened an escalation — SSE streams are dropping mid-response. They get ~12s of tokens then connection closes and client sees partial output. request_id=rid_45b2 region=us-east1 model=redwood-rlhf-13b

Priya: sample repro curl they sent: `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=redwood-rlhf-13b\"` — they say it reliably dies after ~12s.

Sam: thanks — can we grab gateway/front proxy logs for that request_id and the runtime pod logs around the time? also need client SDK version + network (mobile/desktop). ask them for client-side tcpdump if possible.

Priya: asked customer for SDK version (they're on js-sdk v0.7.2) and client network (home broadband, NAT). asked them to run the curl repro and paste output + `--verbose`.

Iris-bot: deploy-bot: Rolled out runtime v1.12.3 to prod at 2026-03-15T14:02:12Z (canary -> 100%).

Alex: hmm we landed a change in the ingress config in that rollout that toggled `proxy_buffering`/chunked handling. SSE is fragile if buffering/headers get messed with. first thing: check LB/nginx/envoy logs for `upstream prematurely closed connection` or `client prematurely closed connection` and for `502` around the rid.

Sam: collecting logs now. running: 
```\nkubectl -n prod logs -l app=redwood-runtime -c runtime --since=30m | grep rid_45b2 -C3
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=ingress -c nginx --since=30m | grep rid_45b2 -C5
```

Sam: found ingress log snippet: 
```\n2026-03-15T14:02:46Z ERROR [ingress] request_id=rid_45b2 502 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 18.203.45.67, server: api.redwood.com
```

Sam: runtime pod shows `write tcp 10.2.3.8:443->10.4.5.6:52312: write: broken pipe` and also `client disconnected` around same time.

Priya: so ingress closed first or runtime wrote error? who initiated disconnect?

Alex: likely ingress timed out waiting for next flush from runtime. We flush SSE data as events, but if the runtime doesn't send headers/initial chunk quickly enough the proxy may decide upstream is dead. check `proxy_read_timeout` and `proxy_send_timeout` and `proxy_buffering off`. Also confirm we are using `proxy_http_version 1.1` + `Connection: keep-alive` for chunked streaming.

Sam: grabbing metrics: Grafana panels show a spike in `stream_disconnects_total{reason=\"upstream_closed\"}` at 14:02. 95p connection duration drops from 30s->11s for that window. Query used: `sum(rate(stream_disconnects_total[5m])) by (reason)`.

Priya: customer attached curl `--verbose` output showing TLS teardown with `recv failed` then `Connection reset by peer`. they also included a short js-sdk trace showing `EventSource: readyState 2` and then an immediate `onerror` that doesn't reconnect.

Alex: for reproductions, ask customer to run this locally (will get more useful client-side timing):
```\ncurl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <KEY>\" \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=redwood-rlhf-13b\" 2>&1 | tee curl_output.txt
```

Sam: we should capture wire-level resets too. run tcpdump on the host nearest ingress for the 1 minute window:
```\nsudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/frost_sse.pcap tcp and host 18.203.45.67 and port 443
```
Note: pcap will be TLS encrypted but will show FIN/RST timings.

Priya: customer can't share pcap due to policy but can share curl verbose + sdk logs. asked for user-agent + client IP at failure time.

Alex: immediate mitigation options:
- increase `proxy_read_timeout` and `proxy_send_timeout` on ingress to 60s
- set `proxy_buffering off` for SSE routes
- add periodic SSE keepalive comment from runtime to avoid idle timeouts (`: keepalive\n\n` every 8–10s)

Sam: pushed temporary ingress config to increase `proxy_read_timeout` to 60s for stream route and set `proxy_buffering off` on canary. monitor.

Iris-bot: deploy-bot: updated ingress config canary at 2026-03-15T14:18:03Z.

Sam: after canary change, the customer's curl repro kept the connection open for 45s and completed. Grafana shows `stream_disconnects_total` dropping to baseline.

Priya: customer confirmed they can now stream end-to-end. asked them to test normal load and report if they see duplicates on reconnect. they reported no duplicates — client resumed semantics OK.

Alex: root cause hypothesis: ingress was closing connections when it hadn't seen a header flush or next chunk due to a recently-introduced buffering/timeout change in the rollout. runtime sometimes stalls for a few seconds when running quantized kernels at large batch start, which exposed the timeout. long-term fixes:
- ensure runtime flushes headers immediately when starting an event stream
- emit a keepalive comment from runtime every 10s by default for SSE and a similar noop frame for websocket streaming
- add an integration test that simulates slow-first-chunk and asserts ingress keeps connection alive

Sam: created ticket INF-1429 to track the runtime header/keepalive change + integration test. linked logs/grafana panels and sample curl repro.

Priya: action items for support: get client `--verbose` curl output, sdk version, exact client IP/time, and any tcpdump if allowed. for prod ops: keep the increased timeouts until fix is deployed.

Priya: I'll update customer and close once INF-1429 has a patch + canary. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Alex: also add a short note to runbook under `streaming/observability` about `how to capture` (kubectl logs, tcpdump, grafana queries, deploy-bot lookups, and common nginx errors to grep). saved snippets:
```\n# ingress errors
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=ingress -c nginx --since=1h | egrep \"upstream prematurely closed|502|client prematurely closed|proxy_read_timeout\"

# runtime broken pipe
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=redwood-runtime -c runtime --since=1h | egrep \"broken pipe|client disconnected|rid_\"

# grafana queries
sum(rate(stream_disconnects_total[5m])) by (reason)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(stream_connection_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

Sam: tagging INF-1429 and adding the ingress rollback/timeout tweak to the incident notes.

Priya: marking this thread resolved for the customer; will track follow-up in INF-1429.

Iris-bot: note: thread archived after 2h of inactivity.
